# Pack: asterix-cat250

ASTERIX Category 250, Test Category for the Generator Tests, edition 1.10 (2020-01-02): one data block holding one record.
Public. Generated by `tools/gen/asterix2pack.py` from the machine-readable definition of the
category in `github.com/zoranbosnjak/asterix-specs` (BSD-3-Clause), file `specs/cat250/cats/cat1.10/definition.json` at commit
`aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`. The category itself is specified by EUROCONTROL. I/O is hex text.
Needs engine version 0.8 (`layout sequential`).

Uses the modules `core` and `cat250` (`model/cat250.def`, generated with the pack).

## Layout

`layout sequential`, `bit_order msb`. One kind, `record`.

| Part | Lines | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| CAT, one octet | `when 8 250` | selects the kind; another category is `no-kind` |
| LEN, two octets | `length 16 whole` | the block length in octets, CAT and LEN included; written on encode, and on decode input beyond it is not read |
| FSPEC | `presence f fx` | bit n is FRN n of the UAP |
| items | one `if f.<frn>` block per mapped FRN, in FRN order | below |

A data block that holds more than one record: the first record is read and the rest of the block is not.

How each item type of the definition is written:

| Item type | Lines |
|---|---|
| fixed | one `field` per subitem, `pad` for spare bits |
| extended | `chain`: the fields of a part, then `fx` for its extension bit |
| repetitive with a count octet | `group <list> count 8`, the body being one repetition |
| repetitive with an extension bit per repetition | `group <list> fx` |
| compound | `presence <name> fx` for the primary subfield, then one `if <name>.<n>` block per subfield |
| explicit (SP, RE) | `length 8 bytes plus 1` with an empty block: the length octet counts itself, so the block is the stated length less one. The content is not mapped |

How each content type is written:

| Content | Transform | Key type |
|---|---|---|
| raw bits, a table of values (enumeration), a Mode S BDS register | `uint` | int |
| integer | `uint`, or `twos` when signed | int |
| quantity with an LSB and a unit | `uscale:<LSB>`, or `sscale:<LSB>` when signed, the LSB as an exact fraction | float, in the unit of the definition |
| ASCII string | `ascii` | string |
| string of 6-bit ICAO characters, octal digits | `uint` | int: the raw bits |
| content that depends on another subitem | `uint` | int: the raw bits |

A key is named after its item and subitems: `cat250.i010_sac` is I250/010/SAC. The meaning of
every key, with its table of values or its LSB and unit, is in `model/cat250.def`.

## Items not mapped

No `if` block names these FSPEC bits. A record with one of them set fails to decode with
`malformed-wire`, and encode never sets them.

| FRN | Item | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | - | spare FRN |
| 15 | I250/150 Wide Register | an element of 72 bits (a field holds at most 64) |
| 18 | - | random field sequencing: the items that follow name themselves by FRN, in any order |

Mapped without content: FRN 17 (SP, Special Purpose Field). Decode reads the length octet and passes over the content; no key holds it,
so encode never writes the item, and a same-format round trip of a record that holds one returns the
record without it.

Items of the catalogue that the UAP read here does not name, and that the pack therefore does not hold: I250/900.

## Shared-model keys

A shared key is bound only where the text of the definition and the unit leave no doubt, and only on an
item that stands directly in the UAP. The text quoted is the definition's.

| Shared key | Bits | How | Text of the definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `speed_ms` | I250/040/GS | `field speed_ms … uscale:463/4096`: factor 1852 folded into the scale; the field has no raw key | I250/040 "Measured Movement", subitem GS "Ground Speed"; LSB 1/16384 NM/s |
| `hae` | I250/050 | `field hae … sscale:381/200`: factor 381/1250 folded into the scale; the field has no raw key | I250/050 "Geometric Height", definition: "Height of the test target above the WGS-84 ellipsoid."; LSB 25/4 ft |
| `lat` | I250/020/LAT | `field lat … sscale:45/2097152`, then `also cat250.i020_lat`: same unit, both keys hold the value | I250/020 "Position in WGS-84 Co-ordinates", definition: "Position of the test target in WGS-84 co-ordinates."; subitems LAT and LON in degrees, two's complement; note: "North and east are positive." |
| `lon` | I250/020/LON | `field lon … sscale:45/2097152`, then `also cat250.i020_lon`: same unit, both keys hold the value | I250/020 "Position in WGS-84 Co-ordinates", definition: "Position of the test target in WGS-84 co-ordinates."; subitems LAT and LON in degrees, two's complement; note: "North and east are positive." |
| `cat250.i030` (the module's own key) | I250/030 | `derive cat250.i030 day_seconds time_ms` in the module: on a conversion from another format the time of day follows from `time_ms` | I250/030 "Time of Day", definition: "Absolute time stamping of the record, as UTC time of day." |

Where a field has a shared key and a raw key, the shared key is on the `field` line and the raw key on
the `also` line. Decode fills both. Encode writes the earliest key that is present (ruling 13 of 0.8), so
the shared key wins: a consumer that changes `lat` sees the change on the wire, and a change made only
to the raw key is not written (ruling 16 of 0.5 asks for this order).

Where the unit of the definition is not the unit of the shared key, the conversion factor is part of
the scale (one foot is 381/1250 m, one NM/s is 1852 m/s, one knot is 1852/3600 m/s), the field holds
the shared key alone, and `model/cat250.def` has no raw key for it: an `also` line shares the transform of
its field, so one field cannot hold feet in one key and metres in another.

Not bound, on purpose: a position, height or speed inside a compound or repetitive item (it describes
something other than the reported target's own state, or one of several); a flight level or barometric
altitude (`hae` is geometric); a heading, or a track angle whose reference the definition does not state
(`course` is degrees true); a Cartesian velocity or position in a local system whose axes the definition
does not state; a polar position relative to a sensor; a time item where the category has several.

## Converting to this pack

The kind has no `requires` line: the definition does not mark items as mandatory, so encode writes the
items whose keys the entity holds. A field of a written item whose key is absent is written as zero.
Keys of `cat250` that another format does not carry (SAC and SIC, for example) are given as context.

## Vectors

Input and expected bytes are computed by the generator from the definition, with a codec of its own;
the generator then reloads the pack and replays every vector through a second codec written from
`spec/engine-spec.md`.

|---|---|
| `01-every-mapped-item-roundtrip.json` | every mapped FRN present, every field of it set, two repetitions in every repetitive item, every extent of every extended item: 59 octets |
| `02-one-item-roundtrip.json` | a record holding only FRN 1, I250/010 (the definition does not mark items as mandatory) |
| `03-extended-items-first-part-only-roundtrip.json` | each extended item with its first part and the extension bit 0; the keys of later parts are absent |
| `04-explicit-items-are-read-over-and-not-written.json` | the same record with FRN 17 (SP) present, each a length octet of 4 and three octets of content: decode passes over them, encode does not write them |
| `05-frn-the-pack-does-not-map.json` | FSPEC bit 8 set (spare FRN): ruling 1 of engine-spec 0.8 |
| `06-category-is-not-250.json` | the first octet is 251 |
| `07-block-shorter-than-len.json` | LEN states 6 octets and the input holds 5 |
